findings.title: Discovery-failure recommendations omit available session-level provenance
findings.what: The panel recommends changing skill README placement or description triggers, but each row renders only the skill, matched keywords, one example command, and an aggregate session count. It does not expose the contributing session IDs or per-session occurrence counts, so a user cannot reproduce the recommendation from the surfaced evidence even though the detector result contains those occurrences.
findings.fix: Add a compact evidence affordance for every discovery-failure row that exposes or drills into each contributing session ID, command, and repeat count, and preserve those fields as structured provenance rather than reducing them to one example plus a total.
findings.acceptance: Given a discovery failure contributed by two sessions, a component test verifies that both session identifiers and their command repeat counts are accessible from the row and that each displayed recommendation can be traced to those exact artifacts.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed that src/components/ToolUsage.tsx:921-945 accesses the occurrence array only for its first command and renders no session identifier or per-session count. The directly related detector result retains sessionId, command, and count for every occurrence, so the missing provenance is a presentation defect rather than unavailable source data.

findings.title: Stale activity data still produces a current-tense trend verdict
findings.what: When analysis marks the cache stale, the component continues to headline HOTTER/cooler and label values as “this week” versus “last week.” A small warning and source footer disclose lastComputedDate but do not demote the stale claim to an explicitly historical “as of <date>” presentation.
findings.fix: When stale is true, replace or qualify the headline and week labels with an explicit “as of <lastComputedDate>” historical label and remove current-tense status styling/wording; keep the underlying values available as historical evidence.
findings.acceptance: A component test supplies a cache whose lastComputedDate is more than two days old and verifies that no unqualified current-tense HOTTER/cooler or “this week” claim is rendered, while an “as of YYYY-MM-DD” label is prominent alongside the historical values.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed src/components/UsagePulsePf.tsx:395-404 renders the verdict unconditionally before the stale-only warning at lines 410-421. The directly related analyzer sets stale after two days but does not suppress or alter the computed verdict, so stale input reproducibly reaches this current-tense UI.
